record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Sublinear WARM equilibrium on infinite graphs
record.original_question: For a WARM, a graph-based interacting Polya urn on a graph G=(V,E) with bounded firing rates p(v), edge counts N_e(t), and reinforcement weight W(x)=x^alpha, suppose alpha < 1. On infinite graphs, is there a unique equilibrium x, and does each scaled edge weight X_e(t)=N_e(t)/t converge almost surely to x_e?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. On infinite graphs there is a unique equilibrium x and Xe(t) → xe for every e ∈ E almost surely.
These problems are devoted to the study of the so-called (W,α)-reinforcement models, or WARMs for short

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a (possibly infinite) connected locally finite graph. To each vertex $v\in V$ associate a "firing rate" $p(v)>0$ with $\sup_{v} p(v)<\infty$ and $\sum_{v} p(v) = 1$ in the finite case (in general assume the rates define a well-defined firing mechanism on $V$). A Weighted Adaptive Reinforcement Model (WARM) on $G$ with weight function $W(x)=x^\alpha$, $\alpha>0$, is defined as follows. For each edge $e\in E$ let $N_e(t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ denote the number of times edge $e$ has been reinforced up to discrete time $t$, with $N_e(0)$ given. At time $t+1$ a vertex $v$ is selected with probability proportional to $p(v)$ (independently of the past); given $v$ is selected, one of the edges $e$ incident to $v$ is chosen with probability
$$ \frac{W(N_e(t))}{\sum_{e'\ni v} W(N_{e'}(t))} = \frac{N_e(t)^\alpha}{\sum_{e'\ni v} N_{e'}(t)^\alpha}, $$
and the count $N_e$ is incremented by $1$. Define the normalized edge weights $X_e(t)=N_e(t)/t$. A vector $x=(x_e)_{e\in E}$ with $x_e\ge 0$ is called an equilibrium of the WARM if it is a fixed point of the mean-field dynamics, i.e. for every edge $e=\{u,v\}$,
$$ x_e = p(u)\,\frac{x_e^\alpha}{\sum_{e'\ni u} x_{e'}^\alpha} + p(v)\,\frac{x_e^\alpha}{\sum_{e'\ni v} x_{e'}^\alpha}. $$

Assume $\alpha<1$ (sublinear reinforcement). Prove or disprove: on every infinite connected locally finite graph $G$ there exists a unique equilibrium $x$, and for every edge $e\in E$,
$$ X_e(t)\xrightarrow[t\to\infty]{\text{a.s.}} x_e. $$
artifact.status_search_result: The sublinear case α<1 is known on finite graphs (Benaïm et al. proved a.s. convergence to a unique equilibrium for finite graphs). The conjecture for infinite graphs—uniqueness of equilibrium and almost-sure convergence of X_e(t) for every edge—appears to remain open in the literature on WARM/graph-based Pólya urns; no proof for the general infinite-graph sublinear case was found.

status_evidence.title: A generalized Pólya's urn with graph based interactions
status_evidence.snippet: For α<1 there is a single point v=v(G,α) with nonzero entries such that the proportion converges to v almost surely (finite graphs).
status_evidence.claim: Sublinear case settled for finite graphs, leaving infinite-graph version open.

status_evidence.title: Strongly reinforced Pólya urns with graph-based competition
status_evidence.snippet: Studies strongly reinforced (α>1) regime and equilibrium structure; does not address sublinear infinite-graph conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Sublinear infinite-graph problem not resolved here.
